summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI advanced-packaging and HBM-backend capacity node. The two-lane list uses TSMC as the reference capacity anchor, then prioritizes underfollowed US-listed second-order beneficiaries: Amkor as the purest US-listed OSAT/advanced-packaging candidate, FormFactor as a probe-card and test-subsystem supplier tied to HBM and advanced packaging, and Cohu as a smaller test-handler, inspection, metrology, and HBM inspection equipment supplier. The node thesis remains a hypothesis: AI/HPC packaging complexity and HBM ramp intensity may create demand overflow, qualification bottlenecks, and higher utilization for packaging/test suppliers, but later layers must verify revenue mix, customer concentration, margin capture, and whether capacity additions dilute pricing power. Expanded the US-listed universe around the AI advanced-packaging/HBM-backend OSAT capacity node. The strongest US-listed direct node exposure is Amkor as an OSAT reference/overflow candidate. The underfollowed discovery lane is better represented by enabling tools and capacity chokepoints: probe cards for HBM wafer test, advanced packaging process-control/metrology, and assembly equipment used in advanced packaging transitions. Non-US reference evidence from Powertech and SemiLens supports the broader bottleneck hypothesis that HBM/AI packaging can crowd out backend capacity and push value into outsourced assembly/test and adjacent equipment suppliers, but those claims require company-specific validation for US-listed candidates.
